message.content:
The hydraulic horsepower relation used in drilling references is:

\[
\text{Hydraulic HP}=\frac{P(\text{psi})\times Q(\text{gpm})}{1714}
\]

Using your values:

\[
\text{Hydraulic HP}=\frac{2850\times 420}{1714}
\]

\[
\text{Hydraulic HP}\approx \frac{1{,}197{,}000}{1714}\approx 698.4\ \text{hp}
\]

**Hydraulic output power ≈ 698 hp**.

This is the **fluid hydraulic output**, not the shaft input power.

question: A mud pump delivers 420 gpm at 2850 psi. Find the hydraulic-horsepower relation in the internal drilling reference and use it to determine the hydraulic output, not the shaft input power.
